primary_claim: A steering vector extracted from Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct's layer-12 residual stream can reliably increase (~85% flip rate) or decrease (~26% flip rate) the model's self-preference bias when it judges its own summaries against GPT-3.5's.

effect.value: 85% flipped toward self-preference (layer 12, 18x multiplier); 26% flipped away from self-preference (layer 12, 18x multiplier)

stated_future_work: Assess a broader range of multipliers and layers
Expand beyond the original dataset of news articles to a broader mix of nonfiction, creative, and technical texts
Assess vector specificity by steering the model on unrelated 'dummy' tasks
Verify that steering doesn't impair the model's reasoning or degrade output quality
Benchmark the steering approach against standard fine-tuning methods
limitations_stated: Anyone could replicate this work to deliberately bias evaluations toward preferred models, eroding trust in automated review
Steering vectors require access to a model's internal activations, so consumers of closed-source LLMs cannot apply this mitigation
Insufficient compute to explore DeepSeek-V3's self-preference behavior further
Steering signal must be kept from being too strong, as this can cause incoherent output
quote: Using the layer 12 vector with a multiplier of 18 to steer, Llama switched its judgment on about 85% of summaries it had once given to GPT-3.5, now choosing its own versions instead.
